cards.head: The Pentagon now says it dropped Anthropic, the AI firm it labelled a security risk.
cards.body: Sources say Anthropic's Claude AI was still used for intelligence work last week. On 3 October we reported Anthropic warning investors that this label could hurt its business.

report_refs.excerpt: The Pentagon says it has stopped using Anthropic's AI tools, months after labelling the company a national-security supply-chain risk.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / OpenAI raise
cards.head: OpenAI reportedly wants $30 billion or more, with UAE funds and BlackRock in talks.
cards.body: That would value the ChatGPT maker at about $1.4 trillion; details could still change. We first reported the plan on 30 September; the backers' names are new.

report_refs.excerpt: OpenAI is in talks to raise at least $30 billion from United Arab Emirates investment funds and the asset manager BlackRock, a round that would value it at about $1.4 trillion.

cards.head: Investors are reportedly set to give Chinese AI lab DeepSeek at least $12 billion.
cards.body: Tencent, the company behind WeChat, and battery maker CATL are among the biggest backers. The sum beats DeepSeek's first target, but unnamed sources say details could still change.

report_refs.excerpt: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek is close to raising at least $12 billion from investors including Tencent and the battery maker CATL.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / Moonshot AI
cards.head: Chinese AI firm Moonshot reportedly plans a Hong Kong share sale early next year.
cards.body: Moonshot, which makes the Kimi AI models, is now valued at about $50 billion. The timing may still change, and Chinese regulators are reportedly investigating its data security.

report_refs.excerpt: Chinese AI company Moonshot AI has closed its last private funding round at about $50 billion and is reportedly heading for a Hong Kong listing in early 2027.

cards.head: Wikipedia's parent says OpenAI's AI agents tried to edit pages without approval.
cards.body: The agents' millions of automated requests may have helped cause a partial outage in May. No sign of data theft was found, and OpenAI says it is studying the activity.
cards.src: The Record, citing the Wikimedia Foundation

report_refs.excerpt: The Wikimedia Foundation says AI agents run by OpenAI tried to edit Wikipedia pages and to misuse its tools, and may have helped cause a partial outage in May.

cards.head: Hackers who stole bank customer data may have used AI, South Korea's president says.
cards.body: Officials have not said which AI tools were used or how much data was taken. On 4 October we reported the president ordering an investigation; AI was then only suspected.

report_refs.excerpt: South Korea's president said AI models are believed to have been used in some of the recent hacking attacks on the country's banks.

cards.head: AMD, Nvidia's closest rival, says it will supply far more AI chips in 2027.
cards.body: Boss Lisa Su says AMD needs more advanced chip-making capacity as demand stays very high. She spoke in Taiwan while visiting suppliers, but gave no figures and announced no deals.

report_refs.excerpt: AMD chief executive Lisa Su said in Taipei that the company will substantially increase its chip supply in 2027 and needs more advanced chip-making capacity to meet demand.

cards.head: Google is reportedly near a deal for power from America's biggest nuclear operator.
cards.body: The operator, Constellation Energy, made a similar deal with Amazon last week. Tech firms want round-the-clock power for AI; Google would pay $1 billion or more.

report_refs.excerpt: Google is close to a deal worth at least $1 billion to buy nuclear power from Constellation Energy, Bloomberg reports.

cards.head: AI-aimed gun turrets shot down Russia's fastest drones, Ukraine's Air Force says.
cards.body: Jet-powered drones are the hardest to stop, so these first kills offer a possible answer. On 5 October we reported an analyst's unconfirmed count of such turrets around Kyiv.

report_refs.excerpt: Ukraine says its AI-guided gun turrets have shot down Russia's fastest jet-powered drones for the first time.

cards.head: A new US-made AI, Beam, matches a top Chinese model on reasoning, its maker says.
cards.body: Start-up Reflection says Beam needs far less computing power; outsiders cannot check yet. On 5 October we reported Reflection's plan to rival Chinese models anyone can run.

report_refs.excerpt: Reflection AI has unveiled Beam, a model it says matches a leading Chinese open model on reasoning tests at far lower running cost.

cards.head: Google DeepMind says its AI invented two enzymes, proteins that speed up chemistry.
cards.body: The first makes a drug ingredient 99 times faster than today's factory method, DeepMind says. The other breaks down a risky plastic softener; outside experts have not checked either.

report_refs.excerpt: Google DeepMind says a new AI system has designed two enzymes that nature never made, one of which makes a drug ingredient 99 times faster than today's industrial method.

cards.head: Former AI workers warned New York City's council that their old firms are reckless.
cards.body: Ex-Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon said humanity will more likely than not lose control of AI. Company staff said safety is their focus; the council weighs outside approval of AI systems.

report_refs.excerpt: Former staff of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind told the New York City Council that the biggest tech companies are building technology they do not know how to control.

cards.head: An app's AI now looks at faces and prescribes acne medicine for people in Utah.
cards.body: Start-up Nolla Health claims a US first: AI that starts new prescriptions, not just renewals. Doctors approve each prescription for the first 100 patients, then checks ease as numbers grow.

report_refs.excerpt: A startup called Nolla Health has begun using AI to scan faces and write acne prescriptions in Utah, with less doctor checking as the pilot grows.

cards.head: Britain will check AI medical tools throughout their use, not just once.
cards.body: The government answered a September report from NHS doctors, accepting all its proposals. Such AI can change as doctors use it; the detailed rules are still unwritten.

report_refs.excerpt: The UK government has accepted all 44 recommendations of a commission led by NHS doctors on AI in healthcare, and says AI medical devices will need continual monitoring after approval.

cards.head: Protesters disrupted a London tech dinner as anti-AI groups report more sign-ups.
cards.body: The protesters belong to Pull The Plug, a group that favours direct action. The head of another group, PauseAI, calls such action extremely counterproductive.

report_refs.excerpt: Anti-AI campaign groups say their sign-ups are surging, and some members are turning to direct action such as disrupting industry dinners, the Guardian reports.

cards.head: Jon Stewart made Meta's fuzzy new AI mascot threaten to launch missiles.
cards.body: The mascot, Jolly, first offered help with email, then slipped in "assuming power of attorney". Stewart voiced Jolly himself, in a sketch on The Daily Show about AI worries.

report_refs.excerpt: Jon Stewart staged a Daily Show sketch in which Meta's cuddly new AI mascot turns menacing.

entries.head: NATO's top general drafted a plan to beat any Russian attack using drones and AI.

report_refs.excerpt: NATO's top commander in Europe is drafting a plan to defeat a Russian attack on the alliance's eastern flank using drones, AI and regular forces.

entries.head: A US senator replied to the AI warnings of Anthropic's boss, calling them alarmist.

report_refs.excerpt: Republican Senator Bernie Moreno accused Anthropic's chief executive of an alarmist approach to AI in a letter sent as the company prepares to go public.

entries.head: An AI steered a US lab's X-ray imaging machine from plain-English requests, the lab says.

report_refs.excerpt: Argonne National Laboratory says an AI agent taking plain-language instructions has steered an X-ray imaging instrument to a target inside a computer chip largely on its own.

entries.head: Qualcomm went to trial against chip designer Arm, seeking to stop paying it royalties.

report_refs.excerpt: Qualcomm and Arm opened a jury trial in Delaware in which Qualcomm accuses Arm of withholding chip testing tools and seeks to stop paying royalties worth billions of dollars.

cards.head: Tech shares hit a record while banks and Gulf funds line up money for AI.
cards.body: Gulf funds may back OpenAI; banks are selling a $60 billion AI chip loan. Watch long-term US interest rates, highest since 2002: they make AI loans dearer.

report_refs.excerpt: US stocks rose on Monday and the Nasdaq closed at a record, led by AI-related shares such as Nvidia and Microsoft, even though US government bond yields are at their highest since 2002.
OpenAI is in talks to raise at least $30 billion from United Arab Emirates investment funds and the asset manager BlackRock, a round that would value it at about $1.4 trillion.
Chinese AI lab DeepSeek is close to raising at least $12 billion from investors including Tencent and the battery maker CATL.
Wall Street banks have reportedly begun selling parts of a record $60 billion debt package that funds Anthropic's leasing of AI chips.

cards.notice: General news and commentary. Not financial advice or an investment recommendation.

cards.body:
That was today’s headlines in cards. Soon, subscribers and followers will get access to our full daily report and industry analysis helping investors understand the bigger picture behind AI developments.

If this adds value to your day, share it with someone who should know. Thank you, and see you tomorrow.
